titulo: Using se debe / se puede to say you must / you can (impersonal)
subtitulo: Aquí se puede nadar. No se debe manejar cansado.
regla: Se puede + infinitive = you can / one can; se debe + infinitive = you must / one must, talking about people in general. The verb is always third person singular.

bloques.texto: To talk about what **people in general** can or must do, use **se** + **puede / debe** + infinitive. In English you'd say _you can, you must_, or more formally _one can, one must_.
**Puede** and **debe** stay in the **third person singular**: nobody specific is the subject.
It's used with verbs that have **no direct object** (**descansar, dormir, nadar, pasear**), or with verbs whose object isn't mentioned (**leer, fumar, comer**).
Tip: **se puede** is the sign on the door: it talks to everybody and nobody.

lista.es: En este pueblito tan tranquilo ==se puede== descansar de maravilla.
lista.en: In this quiet little town you can rest wonderfully.

lista.es: Para llevarse bien con la pareja ==se debe== platicar mucho.
lista.en: To get along with your partner, you have to talk a lot.

lista.es: En mi escuela ==se puede== leer en silencio en la biblioteca.
lista.en: At my school you can read quietly in the library.

lista.es: No ==se debe== fumar si quieres estar sano.
lista.en: You shouldn't smoke if you want to be healthy.
Can you swim at this beach?
You shouldn't drive when you're tired.

secciones.titulo: Not the same as passive se

bloques.texto: This looks like the **passive se** (**se venden casas**), but it's different: here there's no subject that could agree with the verb, so it can't become a **ser** + participle passive.

lista.nota: With a plural object, the passive **se** makes the verb plural: [[6803|passive se with deber / poder]].

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _One must rest after surgery._
lista.r: Se debe descansar después de la operación.

lista.p: Fix it: _En la alberca no se pueden correr._
lista.r: En la alberca no se puede correr.
